## Coverage of the portfolio requirements

The portfolio brief asks that, across the four projects, at least one involves model comparison, at least one involves computational or statistical programming, and at least one uses real-world data. The table shows where each requirement is met, and the bottom row counts the projects that meet it.

| Project | Type | Model comparison | Programming | Real-world data |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| [1: GARCH-X](./project-01/index.html) | Exploration and simulation study | ✓ GARCH, GJR, EGARCH, in and out of sample | ✓ Monte Carlo power study, hand-coded likelihood | ✓ ZAR/USD, Google Trends |
| [2: Spectral Coherence](project-02/index.html) | Exploration and simulation check | – | ✓ Coherence threshold and simulation check | ✓ Eskom EAF, JSE |
| [3: Two-Pot Withdrawals](project-03/index.html) | Implementation | ✓ Poisson vs NB, step vs spline | ✓ IRLS from first principles | ✓ Withdrawal counts |
| [4: State-Space Kalman](project-04/index.html) | Implementation | ✓ Local linear trend vs two restricted models | ✓ Filter, smoother and MLE from first principles | ✓ Banking disruption series |
| **Projects meeting it** | | **3 of 4** | **4 of 4** | **4 of 4** |

The four projects follow one line of enquiry through South African financial and economic data: **risk clustering**, then **external dependency**, then **behavioural response**, then **structural change**. Each card opens a one-page summary, which links to the full analysis.

## How to read this page

Start at the top card and read down, since each project builds on the question left open by the one before. For each project, read the **summary** first. It takes a few minutes and states the question, the key findings and what I would do differently. Follow its link to the **detailed analysis** for the full method, diagnostics and limitations. Code is folded by default, so use the "Show code" toggle to open any chunk, and the hand-coded methods in Projects 3 and 4 are left open.
